findings.title: Wheel and sdist ship a local virtualenv file: hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py installs into every user's site-packages
findings.description: The repo root contains an untracked, un-gitignored virtualenv named hypertools-dev/ (pyvenv.cfg, bin/, lib/python3.14/...). [tool.setuptools.packages.find] include = ["hypertools*"] glob-matches it, and because pyproject packages.find defaults to namespaces=true, hypertools-dev/bin (no __init__.py) is swept in as a namespace package. Both artifacts built by python -m build contain hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py; top_level.txt lists 'hypertools-dev' as a shipped top-level package; pip-installing the wheel creates site-packages/hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py (verified on disk in the fresh 3.13 venv, and reproduced identically when installing from the sdist). Artifact contents are machine-dependent: any hypertools*-named directory present at build time ships. Fix: include = ["hypertools", "hypertools.*"] (and/or namespaces = false), plus gitignore the hypertools-dev venv.
findings.repro: env MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -m build --outdir /tmp/x5dist /Users/jmanning/hypertools && unzip -l /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl | grep hypertools-dev && unzip -p /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl hypertools-1.0.0.dev0.dist-info/top_level.txt
findings.expected: Wheel/sdist contain only the hypertools package; top_level.txt lists only 'hypertools'
findings.actual: build log: "adding 'hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py'"; wheel entry: "2383  07-02-2026 12:30   hypertools-dev/bin/activate_this.py"; top_level.txt: "hypertools\nhypertools-dev"; after install: site-packages/hypertools-dev/bin/{__pycache__,activate_this.py}

findings.title: hypertools/core/config.ini missing from wheel AND sdist: core.get_default_options()/apply_defaults() silently return empty defaults in every pip install
findings.description: hypertools/core/config.ini (the [plot]/[reduce]/[align]/[cluster] defaults that configurator.py documents as 'Central default options for hypertools, parsed from core/config.ini') is not packaged: pyproject has no [tool.setuptools.package-data] and there is no MANIFEST.in, so the package's only non-.py file is dropped from both artifacts (sdist contains zero .ini files). In a wheel install get_default_options() returns {} for all four sections and apply_defaults('reduce', {'ndims': 5}) silently loses 'algorithm' (KeyError downstream); the shipped tests' own assertions (tests/core/test_configurator.py: opts['reduce']['algorithm'] == 'IncrementalPCA') fail against an installed wheel. Impact scoping is empirical: plot/reduce/cluster do NOT read this config at runtime (A/B in the same venv with config.ini restored produced byte-identical plot PNGs, SHA1 c7d0948f...), so breakage is confined to the public hypertools.core configurator API and anything wired through it in the future. Fix: [tool.setuptools.package-data] "hypertools.core" = ["config.ini"].
findings.repro: python3.13 -m venv /tmp/x5v && /tmp/x5v/bin/pip install /tmp/x5dist/hypertools-1.0.0.dev0-py3-none-any.whl && cd /tmp && /tmp/x5v/bin/python -c "from hypertools.core.configurator import get_default_options, apply_defaults; print(dict(get_default_options()['reduce'])); m = apply_defaults('reduce', {'ndims': 5}); print(m); print(m['algorithm'])"
findings.actual: config.ini exists at install: False; defaults[plot]={} defaults[reduce]={} defaults[align]={} defaults[cluster]={}; merged: {'ndims': 5}; then: KeyError: 'algorithm'

findings.title: uv pip install of hypertools 1.0 fails on CPython 3.12/3.13/3.14: resolver picks numba==0.53.1 + llvmlite==0.36.0 (unbuildable)
findings.description: Installing either built artifact with uv (0.9.27) on CPython 3.12, 3.13 or 3.14 deterministically resolves umap-learn's numba requirement to numba 0.53.1 / llvmlite 0.36.0 (2021-era); llvmlite 0.36.0 has no wheels for these Pythons, its source build fails, and the install aborts -- import hypertools then fails. pip on the identical interpreter resolves numba 0.66.0 and works; uv on 3.10/3.11 also picks 0.66.0 and works. There is no true conflict: uv pip install <wheel> numba==0.66.0 resolves the full set (numba 0.66.0 + numpy 2.4.6 + matplotlib 3.11.0). Minimal repro needs no hypertools: uv-resolving the 13 declared floor strings reproduces numba==0.53.1, while bare `uv pip install umap-learn` picks 0.66.0 -- the trigger is this floor set's interplay with uv's pubgrub prioritization. Given uv's popularity with the scientific audience, recommend a defensive floor (e.g. numba>=0.59 in dependencies, or a higher umap-learn floor) and/or a documented workaround.
findings.expected: Installs with a modern numba (pip installs numba 0.66.0 + llvmlite 0.48.0 on the same interpreter) and hypertools imports
findings.actual: " + llvmlite==0.36.0 / + numba==0.53.1" then build failure: "help: `llvmlite` (v0.36.0) was included because `hypertools` (v1.0.0.dev0) depends on `umap-learn` (v0.5.12) which depends on `numba` (v0.53.1) which depends on `llvmlite`"; subsequent import: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hypertools'

findings.title: sdist ships an incomplete, non-runnable subset of the test suite
findings.description: The sdist includes only the flat tests/test_*.py files (setuptools' legacy default 'tests/test*.py' pattern). It omits tests/__init__.py, tests/context.py, tests/matplotlibrc, tests/data/, and all test subpackages (tests/{core,plot,reduce,io,manip,impute,cluster,external}/...). Several shipped tests cannot run from the sdist: tests/test_load_sources.py reads (Path(__file__).parent / 'data' / ...), and test_marker_parity.py/test_multibyte.py/test_story_trajectories.py sys.path-insert '../scripts', none of which are shipped. Anyone downloading the sdist and running pytest (pyproject advertises testpaths=['tests']) gets collection/IO errors rather than the real suite. Either exclude tests from the sdist entirely or include the complete tests/ tree.

findings.title: hyp.save(obj, fname) argument order is the reverse of the np.save(file, arr) analogy its docstring invokes; swapped args give a bare TypeError; **kwargs silently ignored
findings.description: hypertools/io/save.py declares save(obj, fname, **kwargs). Its module docstring frames save/load as 'the same trust model as numpy.save' -- but np.save takes the FILE first, so users translating that habit call hyp.save(path, data) and get a raw open() error naming neither the argument order nor the fix. The **kwargs parameter is accepted and silently discarded (e.g. protocol= does nothing). Suggest: type-check fname with a friendly message, and honor or drop **kwargs.
findings.repro: fresh313/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.save('/tmp/f.hyp', np.zeros((3,3)))"
findings.expected: Friendly error naming the signature, e.g. 'save(obj, fname): fname must be a str/path (did you swap the arguments?)'
findings.actual:
File ".../hypertools/io/save.py", line 21, in save
    with open(fname, "wb") as f:
TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not ndarray

findings.title: hypertools/config.py carries a dead Python<3.8 importlib_metadata fallback under requires-python >=3.10
findings.description: hypertools/config.py wraps `from importlib.metadata import version` in try/except falling back to the third-party importlib_metadata package 'for Python < 3.8'. The package requires Python >=3.10 where importlib.metadata always exists, so the except branch is unreachable (and importlib_metadata is not a declared dependency, so if ever reached it would itself fail). Trivial cleanup: drop the try/except.

findings.title: Build emits SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: `project.license` as a TOML table is deprecated (removal deadline 2027-Feb-18)
findings.description: Every build stage (sdist and wheel) warns that pyproject's `license = { text = "MIT" }` TOML-table form is deprecated by setuptools 83 with a stated removal deadline of 2027-Feb-18 -- builds with future setuptools will hard-fail. Modern form: `license = "MIT"` (SPDX expression) plus `license-files = ["LICENSE"]`. Independently verified in this run's build log (4 occurrences); also caught by the earlier partial run of this unit.
findings.expected: Warning-free build using the SPDX string form
findings.actual: setuptools/config/_apply_pyprojecttoml.py:82: SetuptoolsDeprecationWarning: `project.license` as a TOML table is deprecated ... By 2027-Feb-18, you need to update your project and remove deprecated calls
